s.en: Print network connections, routing tables, interface statistics, masquerade connections, and multicast memberships
s.es: muestra conexiones de red, puertos en escucha y tablas de rutas (antigua; hoy se usa ss)

syn: netstat [address_family_options] [--tcp|-t] [--udp|-u] [--udplite|-U] [--sctp|-S] [--raw|-w] [--l2cap|-2] [--rfcomm|-f] [--listening|-l] [--all|-a] [--numeric|-n] [--numeric-hosts] [--numeric-ports] [--numeric-users] [--symbolic|-N] [--extend|-e[--extend|-e]] [--timers|-o] [--program|-p] [--verbose|-v] [--continuous|-c] [--wide|-W] ⏎ netstat {--route|-r} [address_family_options] [--extend|-e[--extend|-e]] [--verbose|-v] [--numeric|-n] [--numeric-hosts] [--numeric-ports] [--numeric-users] [--continuous|-c] ⏎ netstat {--interfaces|-i} [--all|-a] [--extend|-e[--extend|-e]] [--verbose|-v] [--program|-p] [--numeric|-n] [--numeric-hosts] [--numeric-ports] [--numeric-users] [--continuous|-c] ⏎ netstat {--groups|-g} [--numeric|-n] [--numeric-hosts] [--numeric-ports] [--numeric-users] [--continuous|-c] ⏎ netstat {--masquerade|-M} [--extend|-e] [--numeric|-n] [--numeric-hosts] [--numeric-ports] [--numeric-users] [--continuous|-c] ⏎ netstat {--statistics|-s} [--tcp|-t] [--udp|-u] [--udplite|-U] [--sctp|-S] [--raw|-w]
tip: «netstat -tulpn» = TCP y UDP en escucha, numérico y con el programa. Hoy: «ss -tulpn».

o.en: Show TCP connections.
Show UDP connections.
Show only listening sockets.

o.es: Direcciones y puertos numéricos (sin resolver nombres).
o.en: Show numerical addresses instead of trying to determine symbolic host, port or user names.

o.es: Muestra el proceso (PID/nombre) de cada socket; necesita root.
o.en: Show the PID and name of the program to which each socket belongs.
Show both listening and non-listening sockets.
Display the kernel routing tables.
Display a table of all network interfaces.
Display summary statistics for each protocol.
This will cause netstat to print the selected information every second continuously.
Display multicast group membership information for IPv4 and IPv6.
Display a list of masqueraded connections.
Tell the user what is going on by being verbose. Especially print some useful information about unconfigured address families.
Do not truncate IP addresses by using output as wide as needed. This is optional for now to not break existing scripts.
shows numerical host addresses but does not affect the resolution of port or user names.
shows numerical port numbers but does not affect the resolution of host or user names.
shows numerical user IDs but does not affect the resolution of host or port names.

Specifies the address families (perhaps better described as low level protocols) for which connections are to be shown. family is a comma (',') separated list of address family keywords like inet, inet6, unix, ipx, ax25, netrom, econet, ddp, and bluetooth.
Display additional information. Use this option twice for maximum detail.
Include information related to networking timers.
Print routing information from the FIB. (This is the default.)
Print routing information from the route cache.
